## 1. Monolithic PWA Architectures for Real-Time Fractal Rendering: Perturbation Theory and Sub-Pixel Temporal Filtering in WebGL 2

- **Type:** 2026 Technical Preprint
- **Authors:** Steven Kleynenberg, Google Gemini
- **Date:** 2026-11-25
- **DOI:** https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.15845.77289
- **Canonical PDF URL (630 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/monolithic_pwa_architectures_for_real_time_fractal_rendering_perturbation_theory_and_sub_pixel_temporal_filtering_in_webgl_2.pdf
- **LaTeX Source URL (21 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/monolithic_pwa_architectures_for_real_time_fractal_rendering_perturbation_theory_and_sub_pixel_temporal_filtering_in_webgl_2.tex
- **Abstract:** We present a zero-dependency, single-file Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture for interactive deep-zoom Mandelbrot set exploration in WebGL 2. By combining CPU-side arbitrary-precision reference orbit calculation with GPU-side float32 perturbation delta iteration ($\delta_{n+1} = 2z_n \delta_n + \delta_n^2 + \delta_c$), adaptive sub-pixel temporal accumulation, and deterministic palette synthesis, the system achieves real-time 60 fps rendering beyond IEEE-754 float32 precision limits inside a self-contained HTML artifact.

---

## 2. Integrating the BSP400 neurocomputer with the MetaNet Network Environment (2026 Vector AI Reconstruction)

- **Type:** Author's Re-Typeset Archival Edition (2026 Vector Reconstruction)
- **Authors:** Jacob M.J. Murre, Jan N.H. Heemskerk, Steven E. Kleynenberg, Patrick T.W. Hudson
- **Original Publication:** Proceedings of the 1991 IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN '91), Singapore, Vol. 2, pp. 1476–1480
- **Original IEEE DOI:** https://doi.org/10.1109/IJCNN.1991.170608
- **Reconstruction Date:** 2026-11-25
- **Canonical 2026 Vector PDF URL (76 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/integrating_the_bsp400_neurocomputer_with_the_metanet_network_environment_ai_reconstructed.pdf
- **LaTeX Source URL (16 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/integrating_the_bsp400_neurocomputer_with_the_metanet_network_environment_ai_reconstructed.tex
- **Original 1991 Scan PDF URL (373 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/IJCNN_1991_MetaNet_integrating_the_bsp400_neurocomputer_with_the_metanet_network_environment_neural_networks_1991_1991_ieee_international_joint_conference_on.pdf
- **Abstract:** This article describes the integration of hardware and software components into a single neural network environment. The building blocks described here are the BSP400, a massively parallel neurocomputer with 400 local processing units organized across 25 module boards on a shared communication bus, and MetaNet, a general neural network design tool. Integration takes place using modular operating-system device drivers responsible for bidirectional communication and mapping neural network topologies onto parallel hardware constraints toward a single ideal virtual machine.

---

## 3. The MetaNet Network Environment for the development of modular neural networks (2026 Vector AI Reconstruction)

- **Type:** Author's Re-Typeset Archival Edition (2026 Vector Reconstruction)
- **Authors:** Jacob M.J. Murre, Steven E. Kleynenberg
- **Original Publication:** International Neural Network Conference (INNC 90 Paris), Vol. 2, pp. 717–720, Kluwer Academic Publishers
- **Original Springer DOI:** https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-009-0643-3_59
- **Reconstruction Date:** 2026-11-25
- **Canonical 2026 Vector PDF URL (74 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/the_metanet_network_environment_for_the_development_of_modular_neural_networks_ai_reconstructed.pdf
- **LaTeX Source URL (19 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/the_metanet_network_environment_for_the_development_of_modular_neural_networks_ai_reconstructed.tex
- **Original 1990 Scan PDF URL (635 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/INNC_1990_MetaNet_the_metanet_network_environment_for_the_development_of_modular_neural_networks.pdf
- **Abstract:** MetaNet is a graphical neural network development environment designed to support modular connectionist models such as Categorizing And Learning Modules (CALM). Built on an object-oriented hierarchy of UNIT classes (MODEL, MODULE, GROUP, NODE) and CONNECTOR classes (TRACT, CONNECTION), MetaNet provides interactive 2D workspace zooming and panning, hierarchical detail suppression, subnetwork library reuse, and portable ASCII Network Description File (NDF) export with automated source code generation.

---

## 4. Extending the MetaNet Network Environment: Process Control and Machine Independence (2026 Modern Vector AI Reconstruction)

- **Type:** 2026 Modern Vector AI Reconstruction
- **Authors:** Jacob M.J. Murre, Steven E. Kleynenberg
- **Original Publication:** Proceedings of the International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN-91), pp. 545–550
- **Reconstruction Date:** 2026-11-23
- **Canonical 2026 Vector PDF URL (452 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/extending_the_metanet_network_environment_process_control_and_machine_independence_ai_reconstructed.pdf
- **Original 1991 Scan PDF URL (15 MB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/ICANN_1991_BSP400_extending_the_metanet_network_environment_process_control_and_machine_independence.pdf
- **Abstract:** This paper examines the design of a general, parallel neurosimulator (GPN) capable of supporting evolving neural paradigms and parallel hardware architectures through the MetaNet Network Environment. It frames four core engineering challenges—representation, inter-object dependencies, concurrent process control, and machine independence—and proposes a four-level description hierarchy culminating in a low-level concurrent process representation treated as an ideal virtual parallel machine.

---

## 5. Algorithmic versus Neural Typographic Taxonomy: A Comprehensive Comparative Evaluation of Deterministic Heuristics and Unsupervised Latent Space

- **Type:** 2026 Technical Preprint
- **Author:** Steven Kleynenberg
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Canonical PDF URL (221 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/algorithmic_versus_neural_typographic_taxonomy_a_comprehensive_comparative_evaluation_of_deterministic_heuristics_and_unsupervised_latent_space.pdf
- **LaTeX Source URL (15 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/algorithmic_versus_neural_typographic_taxonomy_a_comprehensive_comparative_evaluation_of_deterministic_heuristics_and_unsupervised_latent_space.tex
- **Abstract:** A comparative empirical study contrasting deterministic geometric contour and stroke-width heuristics against unsupervised neural latent-space embeddings for typographic classification, historical font archival indexing, and structural serif/sans-serif taxonomy.

## 7. Remote Collaboration, Decision Support, and On-Demand Medical Image Analysis for Acute Stroke Care

- **Type:** Peer-Reviewed Conference Paper
- **Authors:** Erik J. Smit, Steven E. Kleynenberg, et al.
- **Venue:** European Conference on Service-Oriented and Cloud Computing (ESOCC 2015), Springer LNCS 9306
- **DOI:** https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-24072-5_12
- **Canonical PDF URL (425 KB):** https://steven.kleynenberg.com/papers/ESOCC_2015_MEDUSA_lncs_9306_remote_collaboration_decision_support_and_on_demand_medical_image_analysis_for_acute_stroke_care.pdf
- **Abstract:** Architecture and clinical deployment of the MEDUSA cloud platform enabling real-time remote collaboration, automated quantitative CT perfusion/angiography analysis, and decision support in acute ischemic stroke care.
